0.original: Qhoterl Pasol wants to give the Stopple a touch of home.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Please note that the difficulty of this quest has been synced to your current level. Furthermore, you may not proceed with a class or job that is different from when you accepted this quest.

1.original: Deliver the requested items to Qhoterl Pasol.

48.original: Ours is a large undertaking, and we expect to be hunkered down here for a good long while. That being the case, I've a mind to add some creature comforts to the Stopple.

49.original: <hex:020815E905FF094D69737472657373FF074D617374657203> <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, I'd be in your debt if you could procure a few things to help me make this place a home away from home.

50.original: Specifically, I require three slabs of slate. These can be had in the depths of Lake Tusi Mek'ta. Many thanks, <hex:02080FE905FF066D6164616DFF0473697203>, and happy digging!

51.original: Specifically, I require three lengths of water ivy. These can be had in the depths of Lake Tusi Mek'ta. Many thanks, <hex:02080FE905FF066D6164616DFF0473697203>, and happy gathering!

52.original: Specifically, I require an eryops. They dwell in the waters of Lake Tusi Mek'ta, and are passing fond of fruit worms. Many thanks, <hex:02080FE905FF066D6164616DFF0473697203>, and happy fishing!

53.original: While there's no avoiding getting a little wet, the slate ought not pose you too much trouble. I await your return with bated breath!

54.original: While there's no avoiding getting a little wet, the water ivy ought not pose you too much trouble. I await your return with bated breath!

55.original: So long as you use fruit worms as bait, the eryops ought not pose you too much trouble. I await your return with bated breath!

56.original: Ah, there you are, <hex:02080FE905FF066D6164616DFF0473697203>. May I ask if you have that which I requested?

57.original: Yes, this is absolutely splendid! My gratitude!

58.original: By making the Stopple more comfortable, our workers will be better rested. And a rested worker is a <hex:021A020203>productive<hex:021A020103> worker! Oh yes, perhaps we can look into extending the length of shifts...
